test_policy.notes: The Elements of a Successful Application page says La Salle 'no longer considers standardized tests for admission or merit scholarships' (test-free). Two other places are not updated: the Founder's Scholarship page still lists standardized test scores among its factors, and College Navigator shows SAT/ACT as 'not required, but considered'. The Elements page is the most explicit statement, so it is used.

requirements.notes: The international FAQ says the application is free; apply with the Common App or the La Salle application. International first-year checklist: official transcripts and school reports from all high schools (official English translations), final transcript and leaving-exam scores if applicable, copies of qualifying secondary exams (e.g. IGCSE, India Class 10), the Common App School Counselor Recommendation and School Report Form, one additional academic letter from a teacher, counselor or administrator, a personal essay, and proof of English proficiency unless exempt. Documents must come from a school official. Living on campus is required for first-year international students.

deadlines.label: Early Action (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: The When to Apply page prints 'November 1' with no year, so fall 2027 entry is assumed. EA applicants get the admission decision, merit scholarship eligibility and need-based aid information in early December (no exact date). The page covers traditional undergraduates; the international page itself says there is no set deadline.

deadlines.label: Rolling admission (fall 2027 entry): no international deadline
deadlines.notes: International applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no set deadline; decisions come within 1-2 weeks after all documents arrive.

deadlines.label: Christian Brothers Scholarship application deadline
deadlines.notes: Application opens in December for admitted students; needs an essay of 500-1,000 words and a recommendation letter. The page prints 'Feb. 1' with no year, so 2027 is assumed. The award amount is not stated on the page.

english_policy.waiver_notes: No proof of English proficiency is needed if English is your native language, you have studied three or more years in an English-based curriculum, or you are from a territorial entity where English is an official language. The international checklist words this as three or more years in a U.S. high school and/or an English-language curriculum. No conditional admission or ESL pathway is described on these pages.

english.notes: Undergraduate (freshman and transfer) minimum. The page does not give a value for the new 1-6 TOEFL scale.

aid.notes: 'La Salle University does not offer need-based financial assistance to international students.' First-year applicants are automatically considered for the Founder's Scholarship (no separate application) and may apply for the Christian Brothers Scholarship. The international page and FAQ give the Founder's range as $10,000-$20,000 per year; the Founder's Scholarship page itself says $18,000-$26,000, so the amount is unconfirmed. International students may also get a housing grant up to $5,000. International students are not eligible for federal or state aid; alternative loans need a U.S. co-signer.

cost.notes: From the 2026-27 Tuition & Fees page. Tuition $40,500 (full-time, all programs). Required fees are per semester x2: university fee $550, student activity fee $200, student wellness fee $150 = $1,800; a one-time $350 orientation fee is charged to fall freshmen. Room and board is a double room ($5,090 per semester) plus the Explorer 15 meal plan ($4,020 per semester) x2 = $18,220; other rooms and meal plans differ (Explorer's All Access is $4,845 per semester)

sat.note: No SAT code is printed on the admissions pages.

act.note: No ACT code is printed on the admissions pages.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is printed on the admissions pages.
